_about: Curated year-by-year supplement written for GeoHistory from general knowledge (conservative: well-established dates only). Each entry names the English Wikipedia article it is about; tools/build_curated.py sets "verified" when the Wikidata item of that article carries the same year. Places are approximate (nearest town).

events.label: Luther's Ninety-five Theses
events.desc: Martin Luther sends his theses against the sale of indulgences from Wittenberg.

events.label: Leipzig Debate
events.desc: Luther and Johann Eck dispute publicly; Luther questions the authority of popes and councils.

events.label: Papal bull Exsurge Domine
events.desc: Leo X threatens Luther with excommunication; Luther burns the bull.

events.label: Diet of Worms
events.desc: Luther refuses to recant before Charles V and is outlawed by the Edict of Worms.

events.label: German Peasants' War begins
events.desc: A wide rural uprising in southern and central Germany, crushed in 1525.

events.label: Sack of Rome
events.desc: Mutinous troops of Charles V sack Rome.

events.label: Protestation at Speyer
events.desc: Lutheran princes protest against the Diet's decision; the origin of the name Protestant.

events.label: Augsburg Confession
events.desc: The Lutheran statement of faith is presented to Charles V.

events.label: Schmalkaldic League formed
events.desc: Protestant princes and cities form a defensive alliance.

events.label: Act of Supremacy
events.desc: The English Parliament declares Henry VIII supreme head of the Church of England.

events.label: Münster rebellion
events.desc: Anabaptists take control of Münster; the city falls in 1535.

events.label: Calvin publishes the Institutes
events.desc: John Calvin's Institutes of the Christian Religion is first printed at Basel.

events.label: Society of Jesus approved
events.desc: Pope Paul III approves the Jesuit order founded by Ignatius of Loyola.

events.label: Council of Trent opens
events.desc: The Catholic Church's council of reform and reply to Protestantism; it closes in 1563.

events.label: Schmalkaldic War begins
events.desc: Charles V goes to war against the Schmalkaldic League.

events.label: Battle of Mühlberg
events.desc: Charles V defeats the Schmalkaldic League.

events.label: Peace of Augsburg
events.desc: Each prince of the Empire may choose between Catholicism and Lutheranism for his lands.

events.label: French Wars of Religion begin
events.desc: Fighting between Catholics and Huguenots starts after the massacre of Vassy.

events.label: St. Bartholomew's Day massacre
events.desc: Thousands of Huguenots are killed in Paris and then in the provinces.

events.label: Edict of Nantes
events.desc: Henry IV grants the Huguenots limited toleration.
